current.text: He is Atlanta's clear starting center. No established backup threatens his role.
Atlanta's center depth is thin. Veesaar is out for the season, Gueye is injured, and Jock Landale is the other center.
Atlanta is reported to be very cautious with his minutes.
He probably will not start the season healthy.
Quin Snyder wants him spaced away from the rim when he plays with Dyson Daniels and Jalen Johnson.
Lloyd expects his lower FG% and lower block rate to stay under Quin Snyder. A FG% bounce back is not guaranteed.
Experts do not expect a big usage jump. His usage fell to 16 or 17 late last season, and the idea that Porzingis leaving boosts his role is overstated.
Experts call rank 49 too high and a round four pick a disappointment. His healthy range is around pick 68, and mock drafters took him between picks 57 and 76.
In an expert auction mock, Josh targeted him at 15 or 16 USD and bought him for 16 USD.
Atlanta plays 4, 4 and 3 games in our playoff weeks and has 14 back-to-backs. Resting players or shutting them down is not a concern for this team.

durable.text: He is a stretch center who shoots threes on real volume. He hit 38% from three last season, and the volume is real even if the percentage dips.
Playing on the perimeter cut his rim finishing and offensive rebounding and raised his assist and three-point rates.
He gave up blocks to cut fouls and defend on the perimeter. His block rate is down, and his steal rate is up and high for a center.
Expect the same block and steal profile going forward, maybe with a few more blocks.
He has very good hands and good feel, and he handles the ball better than most centers.
Not a huge rebounder, but a usable second center.
His balanced line of threes, steals and blocks makes him worth more in category leagues than in points leagues. Plain nine-cat rankings still inflate him.
Quin Snyder runs a high-movement, five-out offense that wants many threes. The switching and blitzing defense puts the center in different spots.

note: Yahoo values him at 22 USD and ESPN at 14 USD, but average costs are 7.6 and 6.7 USD, and he went for 6 USD in our league last season. Experts see him as a pick around 68 and paid 16 USD in a mock, so treat 22 USD as too high and aim for the low teens. He fits any build as a center who adds threes and steals. Early in the season, check his health (Yahoo Q now), his minutes and whether he gets more shots at the rim, since his FG% depends on that.
